articles.summary: Testbed will model and validate integrated fuel cell, battery, and power electronics configurations against real-world AI data center load demand DANBURY, Conn., Nov. 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) - FuelCell Energy, Inc. (Nasdaq: FCEL) today announced its participation in StabilityMax, a three-year collaborative project led by the U.S. Department of Energy’s National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) that will develop and validate integrated power system architectures designed to support the rapidly evolving energy requirements of artificial intelligence (AI) data centers. The project also includes participation from Argonne National Laboratory (ANL). As AI adoption accelerates, data centers are driving unprecedented demand for electricity and creating rapid fluctuations in power consumption. articles.title: FuelCell Energy to Host National Laboratory-Supported AI Data Center Power Testbed in Connecticut Manufacturing Facility
